how can i display the coco collection entries on my website?

**Displaying the `coco` collection on your HaruCMS site** HaruCMS is a flat‑file CMS, so the way you pull collection data into a page is by using the templating engine that ships with the theme (most themes use **Twig**). Below is a quick, step‑by‑step guide that shows you how to create a page that lists all entries from the `coco` collection and displays the `name` and `text` fields. --- ## 1. Create a new page (or use an existing one) 1. **Create a page file** In your site’s `pages/` folder, add a new Markdown file, e.g. `coco-list.md`. 2. **Add front‑matter** ```yaml --- title: "Coco Collection" slug: "coco" template: "coco-list" status: "published" --- ``` * `template: "coco-list"` tells HaruCMS to use the `coco-list.twig` template (see next step). --- ## 2. Create a template that loops over the collection 1. **Create the Twig file** In your theme’s `templates/` folder, create `coco-list.twig`. 2. **Add the loop** ```twig {% extends "base.twig" %} {% block content %}

{{ page.title }}

{% set coco_entries = collections.coco.all() %} {% if coco_entries is not empty %}
    {% for entry in coco_entries %}

  • {{ entry.name }}

    {{ entry.text|raw }}

    • {% endfor %}
{% else %}

No entries found in the Coco collection.

{% endif %} {% endblock %} ``` * `collections.coco.all()` fetches every entry in the `coco` collection. * `entry.name` and `entry.text` are the field names defined in the collection schema. * `|raw` is used if the `text` field contains HTML that you want to render. --- ## 3. Add styling (optional) If you want to style the list, add CSS to your theme’s stylesheet: ```css .coco-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; } .coco-item { margin-bottom: 2rem; } .coco-item h2 { margin-bottom: 0.5rem; } ``` --- ## 4. Preview & Publish 1. **Save** the `coco-list.md` and `coco-list.twig` files. 2. Open your site in the browser and navigate to `/coco`. 3. You should see a list of all Coco entries with their names and text content. --- ### Quick Recap | Step | What to do | Where | |------|------------|-------| | 1 | Create a page with a slug and `template: "coco-list"` | `pages/` | | 2 | Create `coco-list.twig` that loops over `collections.coco.all()` | `templates/` | | 3 | Add optional CSS | `assets/css/` or theme stylesheet | | 4 | View the page | `/coco` | That’s it! Your site will now automatically pull in all entries from the `coco` collection and display them. If you have any questions or need help tweaking the layout, just let me know!
